category_title: Students who disengage when restricted to traditional novels and lack of choice
minimal_context: Lachlan is participating in a silent reading session using traditional novels from the class library.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for silent reading. Please choose a novel from the class library and read quietly at your desk.

STUDENT: No. only books in the class library. They ’re boring.

TUTOR: You need to pick one of these books to read right now.

STUDENT: I like comic books, sports magazines. I don ’t like novels.

TUTOR: We don't have those right now. Just open the novel and look at the words.

STUDENT: (Stares at the page without moving his eyes) Then I would kind of fake read it. Like, look at the words but don ’t actually read it.

options.A: Use desk carrels to provide areas of personal space and make a clear distinction between individual silent reading and group areas.
options.B: Allow the student to borrow books under the teacher's name for use during the independent silent reading session.
options.C: Implement an in-class reward system where the student earns a sticker for his chart whenever he accomplishes the silent reading target.
options.D: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) after each silent reading session.
